text:
Jake Neighbours was one of St. Louis's best forwards last season, 34th of 401 in value by Evolving-Hockey's count, but that number came with a warning: his results ran well ahead of his chances, and some of it was hot shooting or hot goaltending. This season looks like the correction, mostly for his line rather than for him.

His own scoring is honest: 4 goals on 4.0 expected goals, 9 points in 19 games. The problem is the five-on-five picture. The Blues take only 43% of the expected goals with him on the ice, eight points worse than when he sits, and the reason his on-ice goals look fine is luck (8.1 more goals than the chances deserve). That second number usually flips.

Bleedin' Blue put it neatly in a headline this week: he brings the energy, and now the Blues need the goals. His minutes are rising, up over 18 in each of the last two games, both wins. If his line keeps getting outchanced at that ice time, the scoring will not hold.
headline: Neighbours brings the work, the Blues need more
